To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the angular distribution of the road-centerline network in the city of New York, as represented by its GIS database, exhibits a power law distribution, (2) this distribution is a result of the city's growth pattern and its underlying fractal structure, (3) the fractal dimension of the road network is related to the fractal dimension and fractal geometry of the underlying urban fabric, and (4) the road network is a good proxy for the urban fabric.
The angular distribution of road segments in a road network can be described using the concept of angular depth, which is a weighted angular integration analysis.

(i) the angular fractional depth of road networks is a useful metric for characterizing the spatial structure of cities; (ii) the angular fractional depths for different cities and for different urban regions of the same city show a high level of similarity, indicating that the spatial structure of urban road networks is relatively invariant; and (iii) the angular fractional analysis of road networks is useful for detecting and characterizing the spatial structures of cities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
extending the concept of weighted angular integration analysis for the description of urban layouts based on road-centerline data.
the description and analysis of urban layouts according to GIS road-centerline databases.
a new method to characterize and quantify the angular distribution of roads in urban environments.

the proposed angular fractional depth approach provides a useful tool for the description of urban layouts based on GIS road-centerline databases.
the proposed method for weighted angular integration analysis is a useful tool to describe GIS road-centerline databases for urban analysis, especially for the analysis of large scale urban areas.
the angular integration analysis is a powerful tool in urban analysis.

we have developed a methodology that allows us to analyze urban layouts in a quantitative way, based on a syntactic approach, and we have applied this methodology to the analysis of the urban layout of the city of Jerusalem.
we are able to provide a quantitative description of the urban layout based on the angular integration concept.
angular integration analysis of GIS data can be used to describe the urban form of a city, and the results of such analysis can be used as a basis to develop a new approach to urban analysis.

angular integration analysis is a useful and powerful technique for analyzing GIS road centerline data.
the angular fractional depth can be used as a metric for the analysis of the road network in urban areas.

the angular integration analysis of GIS road-centerlines can be used for urban analysis, and that this analysis can be extended from the description of individual road segments to the description of the urban layout in its entirety.
